source.authors: Xie H, Yuan H, Wang Y, Tang X, Yang M, Zheng L, Li Z
source.title: Compound Eye Structure and Phototactic Dimorphism in the Yunnan Pine Shoot Beetle, Tomicus yunnanensis (Coleoptera: Scolytinae)

method: scanning electron microscopy; facets counted on micrographs (counting procedure not described)
conditions: adults collected alive within pine stems or shoots in January-February (year not printed), JiuLong Shan Forestry Station, central Yunnan, China; SEM on detached heads of 10 males and 15 females (Section 2.2) but Table 1 lists n = 14 males and n = 16 females for facet number (unexplained; ranges 224–265 males, 224–266 females); mean ± dispersion measure (SD or SE) not stated; the same sentence gives both sexes (males 240.00 ± 3.51, females 247.38 ± 3.18); no test between sexes reported for facet number in Results (Methods name unpaired t-tests; the Discussion says significant sexual dimorphism in facet number is absent in bark beetles); the preceding sentence states that left and right eyes differ in facet number and surface-area distribution (which eye was counted is not stated); sexes kept as separate records
where: Results, Section 3.1 Gross External Morphology of the Eye
quote: Males possessed an average of 240.00 ± 3.51 facets per eye, while females had 247.38 ± 3.18 facets per eye.
note: new trait: ommatidia_count (key already in use on main). Page prints no licence sentence (metadata CC BY 3.0); one Crossref single-DOI lookup gave CC BY 4.0, content-version vor. Order as printed in the paper's title; family Curculionidae (subfamily Scolytinae) from the original description, Kirkendall, Faccoli & Ye 2008, Zootaxa 1819: 25-39, titled '(Curculionidae, Scolytinae)', as main's desk-d227 row for this paper files it (audit 366). Name filed as printed; Tomicus yunnanensis Kirkendall & Faccoli, 2008, EXACT ACCEPTED in docs/views/gaps/gbif-names.tsv. The same paper's phototaxis result is already on main (desk-d227, behaviour_vision).

source.authors: Xie H, Yuan H, Wang Y, Tang X, Yang M, Zheng L, Li Z
source.title: Compound Eye Structure and Phototactic Dimorphism in the Yunnan Pine Shoot Beetle, Tomicus yunnanensis (Coleoptera: Scolytinae)

eye: central rhabdomere (R7 and R8) of the ommatidium
method: light and transmission electron microscopy of sectioned eyes (Section 3.2.3)
conditions: eyes of both sexes examined by LM and TEM with at least three replicates per sex/treatment group (Section 2); beetles were either light-adapted (LED, 1000 lux, at least 2 h, fixed in daylight) or dark-adapted (complete darkness, at least 24 h) before fixation (Section 2.1), and neither the adaptation state nor the sex of the eyes measured for these lengths is stated, with no length comparison between states; the rhabdom cross-sectional area changed significantly between states, 120.4 ± 18.0 to 152.1 ± 23.7 µm2 (p < 0.001), with cone dimensions larger after dark adaptation (Section 3.3); Table 1 gives n = 6 (peripheral) and n = 17 (central) rhabdomeres; dispersion measure not stated; Table 1 ranges 11.4–12.4 µm (peripheral) and 33.0–55.3 µm (central); one sentence gives both lengths (peripheral 11.9 ± 0.5, central 43.5 ± 1.6) and calls the central rhabdomere 'significantly longer' without a test statistic in the sentence; collected January-February (year not printed), JiuLong Shan Forestry Station, Yunnan, China
where: Results, Section 3.2.3 Retinular Cells and Rhabdom
quote: Within this structure, the rhabdomeres of the six peripheral cells (R1–R6), measuring 11.9 ± 0.5 µm in length, encircle the central rhabdomere formed by R7 and R8 (which is significantly longer at 43.5 ± 1.6 µm) (Table 1).
note: Key rhabdom_um already exists. Whole sentence, seen complete in two WebFetch pieces joined with a single space, including its trailing '(Table 1)' citation (restored by audit 366; 38 words). Page prints no licence sentence (metadata CC BY 3.0); one Crossref single-DOI lookup gave CC BY 4.0, content-version vor. Order as printed in the paper's title; family Curculionidae (subfamily Scolytinae) from the original description, Kirkendall, Faccoli & Ye 2008, Zootaxa 1819: 25-39, titled '(Curculionidae, Scolytinae)', as main's desk-d227 row for this paper files it (audit 366). Name filed as printed; Tomicus yunnanensis Kirkendall & Faccoli, 2008, EXACT ACCEPTED in docs/views/gaps/gbif-names.tsv. The same paper's phototaxis result is already on main (desk-d227, behaviour_vision).

source.authors: Xie H, Yuan H, Wang Y, Tang X, Yang M, Zheng L, Li Z
source.title: Compound Eye Structure and Phototactic Dimorphism in the Yunnan Pine Shoot Beetle, Tomicus yunnanensis (Coleoptera: Scolytinae)

method: calculated, not measured directly: interommatidial angle Δφ = A/R, A the maximum facet diameter, R the eye radius estimated geometrically
conditions: one pooled calculated value (Table 1, n not given); Table 1 gives the inputs as facet diameter 21.0 ± 2.9 µm (n = 130, range 13.5–25.8) and eye radius 481.5 ± 53.9 µm (males, n = 12) and 481.9 ± 45.6 µm (females, n = 12); Section 2.7 describes a second radius method (circular tool at the broadest anterior-posterior point); 25.8/481.7 gives 3.07° and 21.0/481.7 gives 2.50° (auditor's arithmetic, audit 366), so the exact inputs behind 3.2° are not identifiable; collected January-February (year not printed), JiuLong Shan Forestry Station, Yunnan, China; the Discussion repeats the value
where: Results, Section 3.4 Optical Features of the Compound Eyes
quote: Spatial resolution (interommatidial angle Δφ = A/R) was 3.2°; eye radius R was geometrically estimated (R = (s2/4 + h2)/(2h), s = segment length, h = height).

source.authors: Ran H, Li M, Niu Y, Ma A, Yang X
source.title: Anatomy and Ultrastructural Details of the Compound Eyes of the Pear Psyllid, Cacopsylla chinensis (Yang et Li) (Hemiptera: Psyllidae)

method: calculated from corneal-lens diameter and eye radius (87.8 ± 5.2 μm); no formula is printed
conditions: twelve live adults (6 females and 6 males) from a pear orchard in Fanzhuang Town, Zhao County, Hebei, China, collected June 2023, exposed to 1000 lx for 2 h before fixation (Section 2.1); the authors report that electron microscopy of the central eye region revealed no sexual dimorphism and combined males and females (per-sex values in Table S1, not seen); Methods name an independent-samples t-test by sex, but no test statistic is reported; number of eyes measured not stated; the sentence states the angle was determined from a corneal-lens diameter of 15.6 ± 0.6 μm, whereas Section 3.1 gives the cornea as 16.9 ± 1.7 μm in diameter and the cone length as 15.6 ± 0.6 μm (an inconsistency in the paper, not resolved here); the printed inputs do not yield the printed angle: Δφ = D/R gives 15.6/87.8 = 0.178 rad, about 10.2°, or 11.0° with the 16.9 μm cornea, roughly five times 1.9 deg, and the paper gives no formula or other derivation (auditor's arithmetic, audit 366); the value is filed as printed
quote: The total length of the ommatidium is on average 76.0 ± 3.0 μm, while the average interommatidial angle is 1.9 ± 0.6 deg, determined from the diameter of the corneal lens (15.6 ± 0.6 μm) […]
note: Key interommatidial_deg already exists. Sentence seen complete in two WebFetch pieces; the quote is cut at the end, marked […], for the 40-word limit; the cut text is 'and the eye radius of 87.8 ± 5.2 μm.' Page prints no licence sentence (metadata CC BY 3.0); one Crossref single-DOI lookup gave CC BY 4.0, content-version vor. Family and order as printed in the paper's title. Name filed as printed; Cacopsylla chinensis (Yang & Li, 1981), synonym Psylla chinensis, per pestinfo (accepted in audit 287). The same paper's eye_type and polarization records are already on main (desk-d203).
